description: The router is completely unreachable, either from its admin interface or from any connected device, effectively taking the entire network down.
symptoms: No devices can connect to the network at all, wired or wireless
Router's status lights are off, unusual, or all red
Cannot access the router's admin page even from a directly connected device
possible_causes: Router lost power or the power supply has failed
Router has crashed or frozen and needs a restart
Router hardware failure
Router firmware corruption from a failed update
diagnostic_questions: Are any of the router's status lights on at all?
Is the power cable and adapter firmly connected, and does the outlet work?
Was any recent firmware update or configuration change in progress when this happened?
Does a power cycle (unplug for 30 seconds, then plug back in) restore any activity?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check that the router's power cable and adapter are firmly connected and the outlet is working
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A simple power issue is the most common and easily fixed cause of a completely offline router

troubleshooting_steps.action: Observe the router's status lights for any signs of life, even unusual patterns
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Light patterns can indicate whether the router is booting, in an error state, or has no power at all

troubleshooting_steps.action: Perform a power cycle by unplugging the router for at least 30 seconds, then plugging it back in
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Resolves the majority of temporary freezes or crashes causing a total outage

troubleshooting_steps.action: Connect a device directly to the router via Ethernet cable and attempt to access its admin page by IP address
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Tests whether the router is at least partially responsive, even if WiFi or other ports are affected

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the router shows no signs of life after a power cycle and confirmed working power source, consider it a hardware failure requiring replacement
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A router that does not respond at all to power, even briefly, typically indicates a failed internal component

possible_solutions: Power cycle the router
Verify power supply and outlet are functioning correctly
Replace the router if it shows no signs of life after power cycling with confirmed good power
Perform a firmware recovery procedure if a failed update is suspected and the manufacturer provides one
prevention: Use a surge protector or UPS to protect the router from power issues
Keep firmware updated carefully, avoiding interruptions during updates
Keep a spare router on hand for critical networks

description: The router has power and status lights appear normal, but it does not respond to ping, its admin web interface, or any management access attempts.
symptoms: Router lights appear normal, suggesting it is powered on
Cannot ping the router's IP address
Admin web interface will not load, times out, or hangs
possible_causes: Router's software has frozen despite appearing powered on
High CPU or memory load on the router preventing it from responding
Network interface on the router experiencing an issue while the device itself is fine
Recent configuration change causing an unresponsive state
diagnostic_questions: Do the router's status lights look completely normal, suggesting it is powered and functioning at some level?
Can any device at all reach the router, or is this a complete failure to respond?
Was a configuration change made just before this started?
Have you tried a power cycle already?

commands.command: ping <router_ip>
commands.purpose: Test basic network-level connectivity to the router
commands.expected_result: Replies received
commands.abnormal_result: Timeout despite the router appearing powered on, suggesting a software-level freeze rather than a power issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ping the router's IP address to confirm it is indeed not responding at the network level
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Distinguishes a true unresponsiveness issue from simply not being able to load the web interface for another reason

troubleshooting_steps.action: Perform a power cycle even though the lights appear normal, since a frozen router can still show normal-looking lights
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A software freeze often does not affect status lights, making a restart necessary despite appearances

troubleshooting_steps.action: After restarting, immediately test both ping and the admin web interface
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms whether the restart fully resolved the unresponsiveness

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the router becomes responsive again but this happens repeatedly, consider that a recent configuration change or firmware bug may be causing periodic freezes
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Identifies a pattern that may require reverting a recent change or updating firmware to a stable version

troubleshooting_steps.action: Perform a factory reset if the unresponsiveness continues after multiple restarts and firmware updates, then reconfigure from scratch
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Clears any deeply corrupted configuration state that simple restarts cannot fix

possible_solutions: Power cycle the router
Perform a factory reset if the problem persists after restarts
Revert any recent configuration changes made before the issue started
Update to the latest stable firmware version
prevention: Avoid making multiple configuration changes at once without testing between them
Keep firmware updated to stable, well-tested versions
Document configuration changes to allow easy rollback if problems arise
keywords: router ping timeout but powered on

description: The router continuously reboots on its own in a repeating cycle, never staying online long enough for normal network use.
symptoms: Router's lights cycle through a boot sequence repeatedly without ever settling into normal operation
Network connectivity is intermittent, matching the reboot cycle
Problem persists even after waiting a significant amount of time
possible_causes: Firmware corruption, often from an interrupted or failed update
Power supply providing insufficient or unstable power to the router
Overheating triggering repeated automatic protective restarts
Failing hardware component, such as memory or the main processor
diagnostic_questions: Roughly how long is each cycle before the router restarts again?
Was there a recent firmware update, especially one that may have been interrupted?
Does the router feel unusually hot to the touch?
Is the power adapter the original one that came with the router, or a replacement?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if the router feels excessively hot, which could indicate overheating-triggered restarts
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some routers have thermal protection that forces a restart when internal temperatures get too high

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ensure the router has proper ventilation and is not enclosed in a hot or cramped space
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Improving airflow can resolve restart loops caused by overheating

troubleshooting_steps.action: Verify the power adapter is the correct original or manufacturer-approved replacement, providing stable and sufficient power
troubleshooting_steps.reason: An incorrect or failing power adapter can cause the router to brown out and restart repeatedly

troubleshooting_steps.action: Attempt a firmware recovery or reflash procedure if the manufacturer provides one, especially if a firmware update may have been interrupted
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Corrupted firmware from a failed update is a common cause of persistent restart loops

troubleshooting_steps.action: Perform a full factory reset if firmware recovery does not resolve the issue
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Clears potentially corrupted configuration data that could be triggering the restart loop

troubleshooting_steps.action: Consider the router hardware may be failing if none of the above resolves the loop, and plan for replacement
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Persistent restart loops despite good power, ventilation, and firmware are often a sign of failing internal hardware

possible_solutions: Improve router ventilation if overheating is suspected
Use the correct, stable power adapter
Perform a firmware recovery/reflash procedure
Factory reset the router
Replace the router if hardware failure is suspected
prevention: Keep routers in well-ventilated locations away from direct heat sources
Use only manufacturer-approved power adapters
Avoid interrupting firmware updates, ensuring stable power during the process

description: An incorrect setting in the router's configuration is causing network problems, ranging from partial feature failures to a complete loss of connectivity for all devices.
symptoms: Specific network features stop working after a configuration change, such as port forwarding or WiFi
Problem correlates directly with a recent change made in the router's admin settings
May affect just one feature or cascade into broader connectivity issues
possible_causes: Incorrect value entered in a specific configuration field
Conflicting settings between different sections of the router's configuration
A configuration change was saved but not properly applied, requiring a restart
Backup configuration was restored incorrectly or from an incompatible router model
diagnostic_questions: What specific configuration change was made just before the problem started?
Is the issue affecting one specific feature, or has it caused broader connectivity problems?
Do you have a record of the previous, working configuration to compare against?
Would reverting the specific recent change be possible to test as a fix?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Identify the exact configuration change that was made immediately before the problem started
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Pinpoints the most likely specific cause rather than searching broadly through the entire configuration

troubleshooting_steps.action: Revert that specific change back to its previous known-working value
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Directly tests whether this particular change was the source of the problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the router after making configuration changes, even if not always strictly required
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Ensures all changes are fully applied and eliminates any partially-applied configuration state as a factor

troubleshooting_steps.action: Compare the current configuration against a backup or documented previous configuration if available
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Helps identify any other unintended changes that may have been made alongside the suspected one

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the exact cause cannot be identified, consider a factory reset and careful reconfiguration from scratch using documented correct values
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Provides a clean baseline when troubleshooting a complex or unclear configuration issue

possible_solutions: Revert the specific recent configuration change that caused the problem
Restart the router after configuration changes
Restore from a known-good configuration backup if available
Factory reset and reconfigure carefully if the issue cannot be isolated
prevention: Keep a backup of working router configurations before making changes
Change one setting at a time and test before moving to the next
Document all configuration changes with dates and reasons

description: The router is running an old firmware version, which can cause security vulnerabilities, missing features, compatibility issues, and unresolved bugs that newer firmware would fix.
symptoms: Router's admin page shows an old firmware version number when checked
Known compatibility issues with newer devices or features
Persistent minor bugs or instability that firmware updates might resolve
possible_causes: Router has never been updated since initial setup
Automatic firmware updates are disabled or unavailable on this model
User is unaware that updates are available or how to check
diagnostic_questions: When was the last time this router's firmware was updated, if ever?
Does the router support checking for and installing updates directly through its admin page?
Are there any specific known issues or missing features you are hoping a firmware update might resolve?
Is this router still supported by the manufacturer with active firmware updates?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Log into the router's admin interface and check the current firmware version against the manufacturer's website for the latest available version
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Establishes exactly how outdated the current firmware is and what update path is available

troubleshooting_steps.action: Review the release notes for available firmware updates to understand what bugs, features, or security fixes are included
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Helps confirm whether updating is likely to resolve any current issues being experienced

troubleshooting_steps.action: Back up the current router configuration before proceeding with any firmware update
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Protects against configuration loss in case the update process resets settings

troubleshooting_steps.action: Download and install the latest firmware directly from the manufacturer's official website, following their specific update procedure
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Ensures a safe, correctly matched firmware update for this exact router model

troubleshooting_steps.action: Avoid interrupting the update process, including not powering off the router during the update
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Interrupting a firmware update is a common cause of serious router problems, including bricking the device

troubleshooting_steps.action: Verify normal operation and reconfigure any settings that may have reset after the update
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms the update was successful and restores full functionality

possible_solutions: Update the router to the latest firmware from the manufacturer's official website
Back up configuration before updating
Follow the manufacturer's specific update procedure carefully
Consider replacing the router if it is no longer receiving firmware updates from the manufacturer
prevention: Check for firmware updates on a regular schedule, such as every few months
Enable automatic updates if the router supports it and this is acceptable for the environment
Subscribe to manufacturer security bulletins for critical update notifications

description: The router becomes excessively hot during normal operation, which can lead to instability, random restarts, or reduced performance and lifespan.
symptoms: Router feels very hot to the touch, more than mild warmth
Performance degrades or connections drop especially after extended periods of operation or in warm environments
May be accompanied by random restarts or WiFi range/speed reduction
possible_causes: Poor ventilation around the router's physical location
Router placed in an enclosed space, cabinet, or stacked with other heat-generating equipment
Dust accumulation blocking vents and airflow
Router placed in direct sunlight or a naturally warm area of the building
diagnostic_questions: Where exactly is the router physically located, and how much open space is around it?
Is the router enclosed in a cabinet, or stacked closely with other devices?
Has the router ever been cleaned of dust, and how long has it been in its current location?
Does the room or area tend to be warm, especially during certain times of day or seasons?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Relocate the router to a more open area with better airflow, away from enclosed cabinets or stacks of other equipment
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Directly addresses the most common cause of router overheating

troubleshooting_steps.action: Power off the router and gently clean any visible dust from its vents using compressed air
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Dust buildup restricts airflow and traps heat inside the device

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ensure the router is not placed in direct sunlight or an unusually warm part of the room
troubleshooting_steps.reason: External heat sources add to the router's own generated heat, worsening the overheating problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Consider adding a small fan nearby for additional passive airflow if the location cannot be easily changed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Provides supplemental cooling without requiring relocation

troubleshooting_steps.action: Monitor whether symptoms like restarts or performance issues improve after addressing ventilation and dust
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms whether overheating was indeed the root cause of any related instability

possible_solutions: Relocate the router to a well-ventilated, open area
Clean dust from vents regularly
Avoid enclosing the router in cabinets or stacking it with other equipment
Add supplemental cooling if relocation is not possible
prevention: Choose router placement with good airflow from the start
Perform periodic dust cleaning as routine maintenance
Avoid placing routers near heat sources like sunlit windows or other warm equipment

description: The router's WAN (internet-facing) port shows as down or inactive, meaning the router cannot receive any internet connection from the modem or ISP line.
symptoms: Router's WAN/internet status light is off or red
All devices on the network lose internet access simultaneously, though local network communication may still work
Router admin page shows the WAN interface as down or disconnected
possible_causes: Cable between the modem and the router's WAN port is unplugged or damaged
Modem itself is offline or not providing a signal
WAN port on the router has failed
Incorrect WAN connection type configured, such as PPPoE settings that no longer match the ISP's requirements
diagnostic_questions: Is the cable between the modem and the router's WAN port firmly connected at both ends?
Is the modem itself showing normal, working status lights?
Have you tried a different cable for the WAN connection?
Has anything changed with your ISP account or service recently that might affect the connection type or credentials?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check that the cable between the modem and the router's WAN port is firmly connected at both ends
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A loose or disconnected cable is the most common and simplest cause of a down WAN port

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the modem itself is powered on and showing normal status lights, restarting it if needed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A problem with the modem, rather than the router, would also present as a down WAN connection

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a different cable for the WAN connection between the modem and router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out a damaged cable as the specific cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the router's WAN connection type settings (such as DHCP, PPPoE, or Static) against what the ISP requires
troubleshooting_steps.reason: An incorrect connection type or outdated credentials can prevent the WAN port from establishing a link even with good cabling

troubleshooting_steps.action: Contact the ISP to confirm the line is active if the modem shows a valid signal but the router still cannot establish a WAN connection
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out an ISP-side account or line issue as the underlying cause

possible_solutions: Reseat or replace the WAN cable between modem and router
Restart the modem
Verify WAN connection type and credentials match ISP requirements
Try a different port on the router if a spare WAN-capable port exists, or consider hardware failure
prevention: Use quality cables for the WAN connection
Keep a record of correct ISP connection settings for reference
Periodically verify modem and router WAN status as routine maintenance

description: One specific LAN (local) port on the router does not provide network connectivity to a device plugged into it, while other ports work normally.
symptoms: Device plugged into a specific LAN port shows no connection or an unplugged cable message
Other devices plugged into different LAN ports on the same router work fine
Link light for that specific port does not illuminate
possible_causes: The specific physical port has failed or been damaged
Cable being used for that port is faulty
Port-specific configuration, such as being administratively disabled, if the router supports this
Device plugged into that port has its own connection issue, unrelated to the port itself
diagnostic_questions: Does the problem follow the specific port, or does it follow the specific device or cable when moved around?
Have you tried a different, known-working cable in this same port?
Have you tried plugging a different, known-working device into this same port?
Does the router's admin interface show anything unusual about this specific port's status?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a different, known-working cable in the suspected faulty port
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out a bad cable as the cause before suspecting the port itself

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try connecting a different, known-working device to this same port
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms whether the problem follows the port regardless of what is plugged into it

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try the original device and cable in a different LAN port on the router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms whether the problem follows the device/cable instead, which would rule out the port itself

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the router's admin interface, if available, for any port-specific status or configuration options
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some routers allow individual ports to be disabled or configured differently, which could explain the behavior

troubleshooting_steps.action: Consider the port has failed if the problem consistently stays with that specific port regardless of cable or device used
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms a hardware-level port failure requiring a workaround or router replacement

possible_solutions: Use a different LAN port on the router as a workaround for a failed port
Replace the router if multiple ports fail over time, indicating broader hardware issues
Use a switch connected to a working port to regain the lost port capacity
prevention: Avoid forcing connectors into ports, which can cause physical damage over time
Periodically test all LAN ports on critical routers
Keep a small switch on hand as a quick workaround for a failed router port
keywords: one ethernet port not working on router

description: The router's built-in DHCP server feature has been turned off, either intentionally or accidentally, so it no longer automatically assigns IP addresses to connecting devices.
symptoms: New devices connecting to the router fail to obtain an IP address automatically
Devices show an APIPA (169.254.x.x) address or no address at all
Existing devices with a valid lease may continue working until their lease expires
possible_causes: DHCP was intentionally disabled, perhaps because another device on the network is meant to handle DHCP instead
DHCP was accidentally turned off during other configuration changes
Router experienced a factory reset or firmware update that changed this setting
diagnostic_questions: Was DHCP intentionally disabled on this router, for example because a different server or router is meant to handle it?
Is there possibly another DHCP server on the network that should be the one active, avoiding a conflict?
Did this setting change after a recent router configuration change, reset, or update?
Do you want this router to handle DHCP, or should it remain disabled in favor of another device?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Log into the router's admin interface and check the DHCP server settings section
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Directly confirms whether DHCP is currently enabled or disabled on this router

troubleshooting_steps.action: Determine whether this router should be the one providing DHCP, or if another device on the network is intended to handle it
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Prevents accidentally creating a DHCP conflict by enabling it on multiple devices at once

troubleshooting_steps.action: Enable the DHCP server setting and configure an appropriate address range if this router should be providing DHCP
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Restores automatic IP address assignment for connecting devices

troubleshooting_steps.action: Save the changes and restart the router if required for the setting to take effect
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Ensures the DHCP service actually starts running with the new configuration

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test with a new device connecting to confirm it now receives a valid IP address automatically
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Verifies the DHCP service is functioning correctly after being re-enabled

possible_solutions: Enable the DHCP server setting in the router's admin interface
Configure an appropriate DHCP address range if not already set
Confirm no other device is also running DHCP to avoid a conflict
Restart the router if needed to apply the change
prevention: Document intended DHCP server responsibility clearly, especially in networks with multiple routers or servers
Avoid disabling DHCP unless there is a specific, documented reason
Review DHCP settings after firmware updates or factory resets

description: Network Address Translation (NAT) settings on the router are misconfigured, causing issues with port forwarding, certain applications, or devices being unable to properly communicate with the internet.
symptoms: Port forwarding rules do not work as expected for hosting a game server, camera, or other service
Certain applications report connectivity or NAT-related errors
Double NAT may be detected when checking network status on gaming consoles or similar devices
possible_causes: Port forwarding rule configured with an incorrect internal IP address or port
Double NAT situation from having two routers each performing NAT translation
NAT type setting (open, moderate, strict) causing compatibility issues for specific applications
Firewall rules conflicting with intended NAT/port forwarding configuration
diagnostic_questions: What specific application or service is having the NAT-related issue?
Are there multiple routers in the network path, potentially causing a double NAT situation?
What is the exact port forwarding configuration currently set up, including internal IP and ports?
Has this configuration ever worked correctly before, or is this a new setup?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Verify the internal device's IP address has not changed since the port forwarding rule was configured
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Port forwarding rules point to a specific internal IP, and if that device's address changed, the rule will no longer work correctly

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check for a double NAT situation by reviewing the full network path from the modem to the final router
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Having two devices both performing NAT translation is a common source of confusing connectivity issues, especially for gaming and hosting services

troubleshooting_steps.action: If double NAT is found, consider setting one router to bridge mode, or use only one device for NAT/routing duties
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Eliminates the double translation layer that causes many NAT-related application problems

troubleshooting_steps.action: Correct the port forwarding rule's internal IP address and port to match the current, correct values for the target device
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Directly fixes rules that have become outdated due to IP address changes

troubleshooting_steps.action: Use a static IP or DHCP reservation for the target device to prevent this rule from breaking again in the future
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Ensures the port forwarding rule remains valid even after the device restarts or renews its lease

possible_solutions: Correct the port forwarding rule's internal IP and port values
Set the target device to a static IP or DHCP reservation
Resolve double NAT by using bridge mode on one of the routers
Review and adjust firewall rules that may conflict with intended NAT behavior
prevention: Use DHCP reservations for any device with port forwarding rules
Document all port forwarding configurations clearly
Avoid unnecessary double NAT setups by using bridge mode where appropriate

description: The network switch shows no signs of power at all, no lights, no fan noise, meaning none of the connected devices through it have network access.
symptoms: No status or port lights illuminate on the switch
No fan noise or hum from the device, if it normally has one
All devices connected through this switch lose network access simultaneously
possible_causes: Power cable or adapter not properly connected
Power outlet or power strip not providing power
Internal power supply failure within the switch
For PoE switches, a power draw issue if many high-power devices are connected
diagnostic_questions: Is the power cable firmly connected at both the switch and the wall outlet or power strip?
Does the outlet or power strip work for other devices?
Has this switch worked before, or is this a new installation?
If this is a PoE switch, are there many high-power devices connected that might be causing an overload?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check that the power cable is firmly connected at both the switch and the power source
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A loose connection is the simplest and most common cause of a switch showing no power at all

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test the power outlet or power strip with another device to confirm it is providing power
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out the power source itself as the problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try a different power cable if one compatible is available
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out a damaged cable as the cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: For PoE switches, disconnect some high-power devices temporarily to see if the switch powers on with a reduced load
troubleshooting_steps.reason: An overloaded PoE switch may fail to power on properly if its total power budget is exceeded

troubleshooting_steps.action: Consider the switch has an internal power supply failure if it shows no signs of life with confirmed good power and cable
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Indicates a hardware fault requiring repair or replacement

possible_solutions: Reconnect or replace the power cable
Use a confirmed working power outlet
Reduce PoE load if overload is suspected on a PoE switch
Replace the switch if it shows no signs of life with confirmed good power
prevention: Use a surge protector or UPS for critical switches
Avoid overloading PoE switches beyond their rated capacity
Keep a spare switch on hand for critical network segments

description: A specific port on the network switch shows as down or inactive, so the device connected to it has no network connectivity, while other ports work normally.
symptoms: Specific switch port's link light does not illuminate
Device connected to that port shows a disconnected or unplugged status
Other ports on the same switch work normally for their connected devices

The specific physical port has failed
Port has been administratively disabled through switch management, if it is a managed switch
Speed/duplex mismatch between the connected device and this specific port
diagnostic_questions: Have you tried a different, known-working cable in this port?
Have you tried connecting a different, known-working device to this port?
If this is a managed switch, does its management interface show anything about this port's status or configuration?
Does moving the original cable/device to a different port resolve the issue?

Use a different, working port as a workaround for a failed one
Replace damaged cables
Replace the switch if multiple ports fail over time

Periodically audit port status on managed switches
Label switch ports clearly for easier troubleshooting

symptoms: Port shows as 'disabled' or 'shutdown' in the switch's management interface
Device plugged into this port gets no link at all, as if the cable were unplugged
Other similarly configured ports work normally
possible_causes: Port was intentionally disabled by an administrator, perhaps for security or unused port management
Port was accidentally disabled during other configuration changes
Automated port security feature triggered a shutdown due to a policy violation
diagnostic_questions: Was this port intentionally disabled as part of standard unused port security practices?
Do you have access to the switch's management interface to check the port's configuration status?
Has anyone made recent configuration changes to this switch?
Could a port security violation, such as an unauthorized MAC address, have triggered an automatic shutdown?

Investigate and resolve any port security violation before re-enabling
Document the change and reason for future reference

Intentional security policy correctly detecting an unauthorized connection attempt

description: A network loop has been created, often by an accidental duplicate cable connection between switches, causing severe network slowdowns or a complete network outage.

possible_causes: A cable was accidentally connected between two ports on the same switch or between two switches, creating a physical loop
Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) is disabled or misconfigured, allowing a loop to form without automatic prevention
A user connected an unmanaged switch or hub in a way that created an unintended loop
diagnostic_questions: Was any new cable connected recently, especially involving multiple switches or a small unmanaged switch/hub?
Do the affected switches have Spanning Tree Protocol enabled?
Are switch port lights flashing rapidly and continuously, suggesting a broadcast storm from a loop?
Can you identify any recently added network equipment that might have inadvertently created a loop?

commands.command: show spanning-tree (on a managed switch CLI)

troubleshooting_steps.action: Identify any recently connected cables, especially ones connecting multiple switches or involving an unmanaged switch/hub
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Physical loops are almost always caused by a specific recent cabling change that needs to be located and undone

troubleshooting_steps.action: Disconnect suspected loop-causing cables one at a time, checking if network performance improves after each disconnection
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Systematically isolates and removes the specific connection causing the loop

troubleshooting_steps.action: Verify Spanning Tree Protocol is enabled on all managed switches in the network
troubleshooting_steps.reason: STP is specifically designed to detect and automatically block loops, preventing this type of outage from occurring or recurring

troubleshooting_steps.action: Enable STP if it was found to be disabled, following proper change management for a production network
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Provides ongoing automatic protection against future accidental loops

troubleshooting_steps.action: Educate users or restrict the ability to connect unauthorized switches or hubs to the network if this was the root cause
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Prevents recurrence from the same type of accidental misconfiguration

possible_solutions: Locate and remove the cable causing the physical loop
Enable Spanning Tree Protocol on all managed switches if not already active
Restrict unauthorized connection of switches/hubs to the network
Educate users about the risks of unauthorized network equipment
prevention: Always enable Spanning Tree Protocol on managed switches
Label and document all inter-switch cabling clearly
Restrict physical access to network infrastructure where possible

Switch hardware limitation being reached in a growing network
diagnostic_questions: Approximately how many devices are actually connected through this switch and any switches downstream of it?
Has the network recently grown significantly in the number of connected devices?
Is there any possibility of a loop or misconfiguration that could be causing addresses to be learned unusually rapidly?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Resolve any identified loop first, then recheck the MAC address table count

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the table is genuinely full due to legitimate device count, consider segmenting the network with additional switches or upgrading to higher-capacity hardware
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Provides a real, lasting solution when the network has simply outgrown the current switch's capacity

troubleshooting_steps.action: Investigate for signs of a MAC flooding attack if no loop or legitimate growth explains the full table

possible_solutions: Segment the network with additional switches to distribute the MAC address load
Investigate and resolve any network loop artificially filling the table
Upgrade to a switch with a larger MAC address table capacity if genuinely needed
Investigate for MAC spoofing attacks if malicious activity is suspected
prevention: Plan switch capacity with future network growth in mind
Monitor MAC address table utilization on critical switches
Segment large networks appropriately across multiple switches

description: An excessive, self-perpetuating flood of broadcast traffic overwhelms the network, causing severe slowdowns or a complete outage across all connected devices.

commands.expected_result: Broadcast traffic within normal expected ranges for the network

troubleshooting_steps.action: Systematically disconnect suspected loop-causing connections to stop the storm as quickly as possible

troubleshooting_steps.action: Implement storm control features on switches that support them, limiting the rate of broadcast traffic any single port can generate
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Provides an additional layer of automatic protection against future broadcast storms

possible_solutions: Locate and remove the physical loop causing the storm
Ensure Spanning Tree Protocol is enabled and functioning correctly
Identify and address any malfunctioning device generating excessive broadcast traffic
Enable storm control features on switches if available
prevention: Always enable Spanning Tree Protocol on managed switches
Enable storm control as a proactive protective measure
Restrict unauthorized connection of switches/hubs to the network
keywords: network suddenly extremely slow all devices

Port was moved to a different physical location without updating its VLAN assignment accordingly

Verify both intended access is restored and unintended access is removed

Use a consistent labeling or naming convention for VLANs to reduce assignment errors

Align the native VLAN configuration on both ends of the trunk
Ensure both ends of the link are consistently configured as trunk ports
Match trunk encapsulation type on both ends if applicable
prevention: Document intended trunk configurations, including allowed VLANs and native VLAN, for each inter-switch link
Use a consistent native VLAN across the entire network
Verify trunk configuration whenever adding a new switch to the network

description: Spanning Tree Protocol has placed a specific port into a blocking state, preventing it from forwarding traffic, which may be expected behavior or may indicate an underlying topology problem.

STP topology change causing a previously forwarding port to now be in a blocking state
STP misconfiguration causing an incorrect port to be blocked instead of the intended redundant one
diagnostic_questions: Is this network intentionally designed with redundant links between switches, where some blocking is expected?

Is the device connected to this specific port supposed to have active connectivity right now?
Do you have a documented network topology diagram to compare current STP behavior against the intended design?

troubleshooting_steps.action: If an unintended redundant path was accidentally created, such as through an unplanned extra cable connection, consider whether to formalize it as intentional redundancy or remove the extra link

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check STP priority and cost settings if the wrong port is blocking instead of the intended one within a genuinely redundant design
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Incorrect STP parameters can cause the protocol to select a suboptimal port to block, even in an intentional redundant topology

troubleshooting_steps.action: Adjust STP priority or cost settings as needed to guide the protocol toward blocking the intended, less critical path
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Ensures the more optimal or intended port remains forwarding for normal traffic

possible_solutions: Confirm blocking is expected behavior for intentional network redundancy, requiring no fix
Remove an accidental extra link if redundancy was not intended
Adjust STP priority/cost settings to correct which port blocks in an intentional redundant design
prevention: Document intended network topology, including any redundant links and expected STP behavior
Use consistent STP priority settings across planned redundant paths
Review STP topology after any changes to switch interconnections

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ensure adequate spacing and airflow if the switch is mounted in a rack alongside other heat-generating equipment

troubleshooting_steps.action: Consider relocating the switch or improving the room/rack's overall cooling if the issue persists after addressing dust and immediate airflow
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A systemic cooling problem in the room or rack may require a broader environmental solution

possible_solutions: Improve ventilation around the switch's location
Clean dust from vents and internal fans regularly
Replace a failed internal cooling fan if applicable
Improve overall rack or room cooling for switches operating in enclosed spaces
prevention: Choose switch placement and rack design with proper airflow in mind
Perform periodic dust cleaning as routine maintenance for network equipment
Monitor equipment room or rack temperatures, especially in warmer climates

Verify voice VLAN configuration when deploying IP phones

description: A firewall, either on the local computer or on a network device, is blocking internet access entirely, even though the underlying network connection is otherwise working.

Firewall software recently installed or updated with default overly strict settings
Firewall rule accidentally created or modified, blocking legitimate traffic
Corrupted firewall configuration causing unintended blocking behavior

troubleshooting_steps.action: Correct or remove the specific rule causing the block, or reset the firewall to a known-good default configuration if the exact rule cannot be identified
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Directly resolves the blocking issue while preserving as much of the intended security posture as possible

troubleshooting_steps.action: Re-enable the firewall with the corrected configuration and verify internet access is restored

Update firewall/security software to the latest version

Document intentional firewall rules and their purposes
